title: The multiplicative order determines the period of the power sequence
summary: When gcd(a,m)=1, the multiplicative order of a is the smallest positive integer k such that a^k≡1 (mod m).
applies: Integer modulo arithmetic; modulus greater than 1
detail: Modulo 7, 2 has order 3, so two terms with exponents different by 3 have the same remainder.
boundary: You cannot conclude from two equal remainders alone that the difference in their exponents is the minimum period; smaller periods may also divide the difference.
relevance: Explain why repeated modular exponentiation observations are insufficient to uniquely determine the original exponent.
